title: The Clean Safehouse
premise: Private security contractor Jonah Amberdale is hired to quietly guard a disgraced aviation magnate's daughter, Sera Voss, whose father died in a crash the family insists was sabotage. When every digital record of a charter flight vanishes mid-flight — with Sera aboard — Jonah realizes someone inside her own firm is erasing the evidence trail in real time. Following the vanished flight's ghost data, she uncovers a plot to destroy a rival conglomerate's flagship facility with an engineered 'accident' timed to the dawn extraction flight that will carry the conspirators' scapegoat out of the country. Infiltrating the airfield, Jonah must choose between exposing the truth about her late mentor's role in the conspiracy and saving the people scheduled to die; she stops the attack, but the cost is the last shred of loyalty she had left.
about_author: I. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former logistics coordinator who spent six years around private aviation before turning to fiction full-time. Known for procedurally precise thrillers, Reyes writes about institutions that protect themselves at any cost.

chapters.title: The Client Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Jonah Amberdale takes a discreet protection contract on Sera Voss, daughter of a recently crashed aviation magnate, through her firm's gray-market channel. POV: Jonah. The beat is wary professionalism masking unease — the client file has been scrubbed twice before it reaches her.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Jonah establishes the safehouse protocol: no names, no phones, rotating routes. Sera is hostile, convinced her father was murdered and that Jonah is another leash. POV: alternating Jonah and Sera. The emotional beat is friction between two women who both trust no one.

chapters.title: Ghost on the Manifest
chapters.summary: A charter flight carrying Sera's uncle disappears from every tracking system while still airborne — yet lands normally. Jonah pulls the raw ADS-B logs and finds them overwritten within minutes. POV: Jonah. The beat shifts from routine to dread: this is institutional erasure, not a glitch.

chapters.title: The Firm's Quiet Hand
chapters.summary: Jonah reports the anomaly to her operations director, Dane Kessler, who orders her to drop it and reassigns her to perimeter duty. She copies the logs anyway. POV: Jonah. The beat is the first crack of betrayal — her own employer is complicit or afraid.

chapters.title: What Sera Remembers
chapters.summary: Sera reveals her father spent his final week shredding documents and muttering about 'the dawn schedule.' She gives Jonah a burner he hid in her childhood piano. POV: Sera. The beat is grief converting into purpose; the alliance begins.

chapters.title: Six Minutes of Silence
chapters.summary: Reconstructing the vanished flight, Jonah finds a six-minute transponder gap over unmarked land — long enough for a cargo transfer nobody logged. POV: Jonah. The beat is cold clarity: the flight wasn't erased to hide where it went, but what it carried.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Ledger
chapters.summary: The burner unlocks encrypted files from Ruth Calloway, Jonah's late mentor, showing payments routed through the firm to an airfield called Merrow Point. POV: split Jonah/flashback-Ruth. The beat is devastating doubt — the woman who taught Jonah everything may have built this.

chapters.title: Merrow Point
chapters.summary: Jonah surveils Merrow Point airfield under a maintenance cover identity, cataloging hangars, fuel depots, and a private terminal booked for a single dawn departure. POV: Jonah. The beat is hunter's patience sharpening into alarm as she maps the extraction timeline.

chapters.title: Kessler's Offer
chapters.summary: Kessler confronts Jonah with proof he knows she's been digging — then offers her a place in the plan: silence now, partnership after. He frames it as loyalty to the firm that made her. POV: Jonah. The beat is temptation with teeth; refusing means becoming a target.

chapters.title: Scapegoat
chapters.summary: Decoded files reveal the dawn flight's real passenger: a fall-guy pilot who believes he's flying a routine charter, set to take the blame for tomorrow's 'accident.' POV: the pilot, Elias Brandt. The beat is tragic irony — the patsy packing his bag, grateful for the work.

chapters.title: The Target Beneath
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing cargo manifests, Jonah identifies the target: Halcyon Grid's regional control facility, whose failure would be staged as equipment malfunction during a scheduled maintenance window. POV: Jonah. The beat is horror at scale — thousands of lives reduced to a line item.

chapters.title: Loyalty Audit
chapters.summary: Jonah tests her own team, feeding each member a different version of the Merrow Point story to find who leaks to Kessler. One does: her closest colleague, Tomas. POV: Jonah. The beat is loneliness deepening — even her chosen family has a price.

chapters.title: Ruth's Last Flight
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Ruth Calloway's final weeks, showing how she discovered the plot, tried to stop it, and died in the 'accident' that killed Sera's father. POV: Ruth. The beat is tragic revelation — Ruth's death was the conspiracy's rehearsal.

chapters.title: Seventeen Hours
chapters.summary: With seventeen hours until the dawn extraction, Jonah lays out the attack timeline: sabotage crews move at midnight, the grid fails at 3 a.m., the plane leaves at first light. POV: Jonah. The beat is controlled urgency — a clock now governs every choice.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Falls
chapters.summary: Kessler's cleaners hit the safehouse to erase Sera and the burner. Jonah and Sera escape through storm drains seconds ahead, but the evidence copies burn. POV: alternating. The beat is terror and fury — they are now officially ghosts.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: On the run, Jonah makes an uneasy pact with a Halcyon Grid insider who confirms the maintenance window and agrees to delay it — buying hours, not certainty. POV: the insider, Mara Chen. The beat is fragile trust between strangers with everything to lose.

chapters.title: Elias Brandt's Choice
chapters.summary: Jonah reaches the scapegoat pilot before departure and shows him what he's really carrying. Brandt, ruined and desperate, agrees to fly the mission — but on Jonah's terms. POV: Brandt. The beat is redemption offered to a man who assumed he deserved none.

chapters.title: Midnight at Merrow Point
chapters.summary: Jonah infiltrates the airfield during the sabotage crew's arrival, planting herself between the conspirators and their exit. Kessler arrives to oversee the extraction personally. POV: Jonah. The beat is coiled stillness before violence — everyone is finally in one room.

chapters.title: Dawn Extraction
chapters.summary: Climax: the grid attack fails thanks to Mara's delay, forcing Kessler to accelerate the flight. Jonah sabotages the aircraft's clearance, confronts Kessler on the tarmac, and forces him to confess on an open channel as federal agents — tipped by Brandt's mayday — descend. POV: Jonah. The beat is explosive confrontation and moral victory at gunpoint.

chapters.title: The Cost of Clean
chapters.summary: In custody, Kessler reveals Ruth chose to die rather than name Jonah as leverage — the final gift and wound. Jonah realizes her loyalty was never betrayed; it was spent protecting her all along. POV: Jonah. The beat is grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Jonah testifies before investigators, dismantling the firm brick by brick while Sera watches from the gallery. The conglomerate's corruption becomes public record. POV: Sera. The beat is quiet vindication — truth outlasting power.

chapters.title: The Next Contract
chapters.summary: Jonah rebuilds as an independent, taking only clients she can look in the eye. A new file arrives with familiar redactions — and this time she opens it knowing exactly what she's walking into. POV: Jonah. The beat is hardened resolve: the work continues, but on her terms.
